discipline: Refute, do not confirm. This subject is a single-finding successor: v8 died dual REJECT 0/1 on G21LJ-V8-SF1, and v9's entire warrant is that it lands that one finding without disturbing anything else. So the review was run as two separate attacks rather than one read. First, the repair was attacked for being cosmetic: the exact defective field was located by path, the v8 and v9 texts were set side by side, and the remedy both v8 reviewers demanded was checked literally against what v9 wrote. Second, and more importantly, the UNCHANGED body was attacked, because a one-field successor is exactly where a reviewer is tempted to inherit v8's dual finding of zero MUST-FIX and stop reading. That inheritance was refused: v8 and v9 were flattened to leaf paths and diffed key-by-key so that every carried field was identified explicitly, and then the carried claims were re-derived from primary sources rather than from v8's verdict. Every digest anywhere in the document was recomputed from disk. The load-bearing counts were re-derived physically — the fixture tree was listed to confirm the eight platform copies the subject asserts actually exist and that no Windows directory was created, and the twenty-three-class remainder was recomputed as named-minus-authored rather than read off the subject. The occupancy v4 passProperty was read in full and set against the subject's rendition, because a truncation of that clause was the evidentiary core of the finding this lineage landed at v6 and a successor is where such a truncation would silently reappear. The subject was swept a final time for any residual sentence, anywhere, still asserting in the present tense that leftover-design of the platform copies remains — the negation the whole lineage has been chasing since v5.
decisionRule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX stand, so the verdict is ACCEPT.

A successor's repair cannot be adversarially tested without the charge it answers. That is lineage evidence about a frozen artifact, not knowledge of any reviewer's position on this v9.
